title: Confront the Brutal Facts
coreMove: Build a room where hard facts can enter without becoming despair or blame.
sourcePressure: The source pairs brutal facts with the Stockdale paradox and supports question-led leadership, debate, autopsies without blame, and red-flag mechanisms.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version confuses candor with cruelty or faith with denial.

hook: boss slams bad numbers on a table

exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse manager whose unit is proud of survival rates
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small infection cluster could become fatal if staff protect feelings over facts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager asks three questions before offering any answer, then places anonymous line-access timestamps on the huddle rail so debate starts with facts, not blame
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tiny name bands clipped beside a sink timer at dawn

exampleSpecs.audience: a bank president seeing early stress in farm equipment loans
exampleSpecs.stakes: denial could damage borrowers and the bank before harvest receipts arrive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the president hands each lender a red card they can raise when optimism outruns evidence, then keeps the card raised for his own favorite borrower
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red index cards beside a tray of stamped loan folders

exampleSpecs.audience: a patrol leader deciding whether to open a high bowl after new snow
exampleSpecs.stakes: ticket pressure is rising while a weak layer still sits under the slope
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the leader asks each patroller what evidence would change their mind before slicing the snow pit and watching the slab shear cleanly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a snow saw teeth-down across a blue shadow in the pit wall

exampleSpecs.audience: an artistic director whose loyal patrons still praise the season
exampleSpecs.stakes: applause hides a shrinking base that could close the second stage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director runs an autopsy without blame by pinning empty-seat maps beside patron praise letters and asking what both can be true
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a row map dotted with gray empty-seat stickers

exampleSpecs.audience: a pantry director who hears only the smooth weekly volunteer report
exampleSpecs.stakes: families are being turned away quietly while volunteers protect the director from discouraging news
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director installs a brass counter bell for every turned-away family and lets the sound interrupt the packing line until the waitlist is visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass service bell beside torn produce boxes

exampleSpecs.audience: a maintenance supervisor after a nonfatal inspection miss
exampleSpecs.stakes: mechanics will hide future misses if the review becomes punishment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the supervisor asks what made the wrong torque setting easy to choose, then labels the socket tray and signoff screen as system facts before naming any person
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a torque wrench lying on a foam tray with one empty cutout

skillTargets: pair hard evidence with continued resolve
distinguish red-flag mechanisms from complaint boxes

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next decision, write one question that would let bad news enter the room and one sentence that keeps the team from treating that news as defeat.

sourceAnchors.name: Stockdale
sourceAnchors.detail: the source names the Stockdale paradox as confronting current facts without flinching while maintaining faith in eventual success
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Stockdale paradox keeps the room from choosing between clean facts and a living future.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
